# Cully 0.20.0

- **Keep work on track.** Task-aware checkpoints ask for direction when a session repeats failures, spends 20 read/search calls exploring without an edit or check, or makes 12 edits without a successful check. Repeated full reads of unchanged files also get a nudge. Checkpoints are deduplicated and respect task boundaries; hooks provide guidance without changing agent permissions.
- **Bound automatic advisor work.** Each Cully session admits at most six automatic requests per rolling hour, with a two-minute cooldown and suppression of identical evidence. Status explains deferrals and local warnings remain available. Four advisor sessions can run concurrently, preserving ordering within each session, so one slow request does not stall every session.
- **Show gaps in the evidence.** Session reports disclose incomplete journal history and missing agent signals. Cursor shell outcomes stay unknown when the host does not report success, and do not become passing checks. Advice uses the active agent and the accepted task title.
- **Test the evaluators themselves.** Deliberately broken installers, audits, monitors and retrieval stores must fail. Duplicate retrieval results cannot inflate scores, unseeded results count toward precision, and an explicitly requested live evaluation fails when it cannot run.
- **A clearer harness workflow.** Solo is the coding-agent harness runtime; Team is the project management harness runtime for people and AI agents building software. Bundled skills guide prompt understanding, planning, existing authorization, implementation, advisor consultation and verification, with scope and budget guardrails. The harness research and current limits are documented.
- **Complete plugin installation notes.** Release notes now include tag-pinned plugin installation commands through the release workflow.

Update with `cully update --version v0.20.0`, or use the [installer](https://docs.cully.net/installation). Rerun `cully setup` with your original options to refresh installed hooks and skills.

The checkpoints are advisory and depend on available host signals. Skill guidance is not a universal enforced approval gate. Automatic advisor request limits are not a hard cap on coding-agent tokens or billing; explicit rescue and live evaluations are outside that automatic budget. See [guardrails](https://docs.cully.net/guardrails) and the [harness review](https://docs.cully.net/harness-review).
